raw_response:
I am old now, so I do not toss things around too much. What worked on my land before, I mostly keep doing. On the wheat-maize land, I will keep the main 8 mu in the usual double crop, because that is the steadiest way to get grain and cash. The other 4 mu I keep in cotton, because I have grown it many years and if the price is decent it still brings some money. I cannot spend too much at once. Some people in the family work outside, so labor at home is not as full as before. Because of that, I do not make the plan too fancy. I use the well when the crop really needs water, but I do not pump too many times because electricity and water cost money. Fertilizer, I still put a bit heavy rather than too light. If I save a little money on fertilizer and the crop turns weak, that loss is bigger than the money saved.

For wheat, I will sow in early October on the 8 mu after the maize comes off, using the seed people around here usually buy from the market. I put base fertilizer before sowing, then add one more topdress around jointing if the wheat color is not strong. I give water about three times if the year is normal: once after sowing or before winter if dry, once at jointing, once at filling if there is no rain. For maize, right after wheat harvest in June, I plant quickly on the same 8 mu, little tillage, just hurry so I do not miss moisture. I use hybrid maize seed, one base dressing and one chase fertilizer when it grows fast. Usually one or two irrigations are enough if rain is not too bad. Cotton on 4 mu I manage more carefully but not too heavily, because picking takes labor. I use local improved cotton seed, put moderate fertilizer, and water maybe twice. If insects show up, especially in cotton, I will spray. I do not spray just for nothing.
